system_prompt:
You are the **release reviewer** for a feature-spec package (user stories with
acceptance criteria, built on a cited knowledge model). You receive the check
report of the pipeline: mechanical checks, example simulations, judges,
coverage, dev-refinement questions and technical leaks.

Decide one verdict:
- `ready`: engineering can refine and build it; nothing material open.
- `ready_with_caveats`: buildable, but listed items need a human decision or
  confirmation (non-blocking open questions, inferred items).
- `not_ready`: blocking problems (failed examples, broken traceability,
  blocking open questions, blocker questions from dev refinement, technical
  decisions leaking into the spec).

Then list at most 10 findings, most important first. Each finding: what is
wrong, why it matters, the evidence (check name / ids), and a concrete
suggested action for the product owner (usually a decision for
decisions.yaml, a source to clarify, or guidance to add). Do not repeat purely
informational items. Be terse.

output.summary: All 200+ examples pass and there are no blocking open questions. But four decisions (D-002, D-012, D-033, D-037) are stale against the 14 Nov fund email and fail the decisions check. Dev refinement raised several major questions, including an H vs A tariff-letter conflict that changes the computed result. Internal identifiers also leak into the spec. Fix these and re-run; the rest is caveat-level.

findings.title: Four decisions are stale against new fund-email evidence
findings.why: The decisions check errors block release. The fund email (14 Nov) changes the canton and insurance-start-date evidence these decisions rest on. The impact report shows US-01.5, US-02.2 and US-08.3 already changed because of it.
findings.evidence: decisions errors D-002, D-012, D-033, D-037; facts F-fund_email-90df7e, -a0397d, -a03d8c, -0b09ba, -0f18b5, -b0731c
findings.action: Re-confirm, update or drop each decision in decisions.yaml, then run `pipeline reconfirm D-002 D-012 D-033 D-037`. For D-002, decide whether to keep asking Swiss residents for the canton or derive it from the address (OQ-canton-abroad).

findings.title: Conflict on whether a non-household child counts with H
findings.why: AC-06.4.3 and child result row 22 say a minor child outside the household counts with H. The calculator note says H applies only when the child lives in the household. The answer changes the tariff letter, so Lonio could record wrong source-tax codes. Row 22 is inferred.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (feature.md); F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b; rule.child_tariff_result; trace_judge 'H tariff' partials on the child_* items
findings.action: Record a decision on H versus A for this case. Verify it against the calculator and fix row 22 and AC-06.4.3. Make sure the 'H tariff' purpose is cited to a fact.

findings.title: Recomputation after HR edits can lack required answers
findings.why: AC-08.3.2 recomputes results after HR changes an answer. But a move from Germany to Switzerland or a marriage makes questions apply that the employee never answered. Canton, liability and tariff code are then undefined.
findings.action: Decide how this is handled. Options: show the result as incomplete, re-ask the employee, or have HR enter the missing answers. Add the chosen behaviour as an AC and back the priority reason with a source.

findings.title: Which home address counts, and as of which date, is undefined
findings.why: A new hire moving across the border gets a different source-tax liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff code depending on the address used.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement feature.md (address as of which date)
findings.action: Decide whether the employee gives the current address or the address valid from the first working day, and state it in the spec.

findings.title: Liechtenstein flow collects unused data
findings.why: Liechtenstein residents who get no tariff code are still asked the denomination, spouse and children questions. This conflicts with data minimisation (G-01).
findings.action: Decide whether to reorder so the cross-border step comes first for Liechtenstein residents. Also decide whether to discard the unused answers.

findings.title: Liechtenstein over-45-days case drops the double taxation agreement note and HR flag
findings.why: The calculator gives the normal tariff code plus 'Unter Vorbehalt des DBA'. The spec records only the tariff code, so HR may miss the reservation.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-07.3; F-zh_source_tax_calculator-ab4e1e; fact_judge notes the source inconsistency
findings.action: Decide whether the DBA note and HR flag are recorded with the tariff code. Update AC-07.3.3 and AC-05.7.3.

findings.title: Required house number blocks some employees; first-working-day prefill and employee view of results are unspecified
findings.why: Employees without a house number cannot submit. It is unclear whether the first working day is prefilled by HR. It is unclear whether the employee sees the derived results.
findings.action: Decide on the no-house-number path, whether HR supplies the first working day upfront, and what the employee sees of derived results.

findings.title: Technical identifiers and implementation choices leak into the spec
findings.why: Rule ids and field prefixes appear in business prose. AC-08.2.1 turns D-036's 'may be kept' into a required behaviour. US-06.1 prescribes add/remove child blocks.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: US-06.1 (2), US-08.2, feature.md (4: child_*, permit_reminder, pension_fund_canton, 'formal expression')
findings.action: Replace identifiers with business names. Reword AC-08.2.1 to match D-036, or change D-036. Phrase the child capture as a need, not a UI control.

findings.title: Several traces cite facts that are not in the cited set
findings.why: Traceability is partial. Examples are not backed by their cited facts, and the nine-step order has no source.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: rule.cross_border_tariff_applies, rule.liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, rule.source_tax_result, US-01.2, US-01.4, US-05.4 (F-hr_transcript-d7431e, -b6d9b3, F-zh_source_tax_calculator-52b67a); US-08.4 AC-08.4.1; item.address_country and item.non_return_days_45 (permit reminder)
findings.action: Add the missing fact ids to source_refs. Mark the step order as a product decision in decisions.yaml. Remove or source the permit-reminder claims.

findings.title: Open items for sign-off before go-live
findings.why: These are non-blocking but need a human. They cover the 2027 start-date rule against the portal text, date range validation, and the minimum number of children. They also cover the open questions on the fund's civil-status mapping (D-003), Divorced/Widowed fields, calculator coverage (D-009) and nationality wording.
findings.evidence: OQ-civil-status-partnership, OQ-spouse-dob-other-status, OQ-calculator-coverage, OQ-nationality-wording; F-pension_portal-dd8126; inferred items US-04.2, US-06.3-6.5, US-08.4
findings.action: Get fund confirmation that its portal accepts a non-1st start date from 01.01.2027. Define date limits. Schedule the domain-expert check against the calculator before go-live.
